title: Record Scratch
blurb: The record scratch — the sound that stops time. Fused permanently to the freeze-frame and "yep, that's me — you're probably wondering how I got here," it's the universal signal that a story is about to rewind to explain itself. The trick works because a needle dragging across vinyl is genuinely jarring: it interrupts music, which is to say it interrupts expectation. Use it to cut someone off mid-sentence, to open a story at its worst possible moment, or whenever a scene needs to visibly stop and reconsider itself.
origin: The vinyl-scratch interrupt, canonized by the freeze-frame narration trope.
